text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Jordanian soldier sentenced to life in prison for killing seven Israeli schoolgirls in March.
- Israeli Labour party leader Ehud Barak says no to unity government.
- Dentists' AIDS guidelines updated.
- Government to review Maccabiah bridge collapse.
- Cabinet to debate Palestinian Authority police terrorism.
- Army simulation game to take over Palestinian cities ends in huge number of casualties, meaning it's unlikely to be implemented.
HAARETZ
- National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon working to change the law so that 61 -- rather than current 80 -- members of Knesset could oust a prime minister without forcing Knesset elections.
- Government hospital workers to strike for a day on Monday.
- Dispute in Knesset over proposed cuts in their salaries and benefits.
- United States in tough message to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat: We'll not accept Palestinian Authority involvement in terrorism.
- Majority of cabinet ministers support cut of 600 million shekels in budget.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- "Evidence for six indictments in collapse" of Maccabiah bridge in which two Australians died. Allegation is deaths caused through negligence.
- Palestinians arrest four policemen who belonged to terrorist group.
- In the Treasury it's estimated the 1997 deficit will be greater than the target set.
- Yaacov Katz will be appointed director-general of the National Infrastructure ministry.
MAARIV
- Contacts aim to arrange a meeting of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.
($1 = 3.53 shekels)
